summary: Round 3, verify only. Four of the five folded-in fixes close the mutation they name: TR2-M4.8-1 (decode what was PUT, per-stream/per-pod values against a differing workload, distinct keys across two triggers) kills both the constant/stale body and the constant seq; TR2-M4.8-2 now names chainEnd AND applyChain with applyChain as the worse site; TR2-M4.8-3 mirrors the K boundary for T two-sided (T-epsilon zero / T+epsilon one kills period=T.multipliedBy(2) and dividedBy(2)) and adds the T=0 failure path; TR2-M4.8-4 now carries the ~38 KiB magnitude and its cross-reference to M4.8c's page-count clause resolves. TR2-M4.8-5's correction is stated correctly -- but the INVERTED sentence it corrects is still in the same row, two clauses later, asserted as measured history. The production reviewer's M4.8-R2a is fixed in one copy and not in its duplicate, which is the exact failure the M4.8 banner in this same commit names as its lesson.

findings.title: The corrected measurement is right; the INVERTED copy of it survives two clauses later in the same row, asserted as measured history
findings.failure_scenario: M4.8a's row now states the M4.1 figure twice, in opposite directions. Correct, first: 'M4.1 records that at THREE streams a broken sort still produced the asserted order about 1 run in 6, i.e. it was killed roughly 5 runs in 6 and SURVIVED 1.' That matches M4.1's landed row verbatim (backlog-done.md: 'at three streams a broken sort still produced the asserted order about 1 run in 6'). Inverted, still present at the end of the ENTRY-COUNT clause and introduced by the words that make it authoritative: 'That is measured history here, not theory -- M4.1's row records the missing-sort mutation KILLED about 1 run in 6 at three streams, and 8 of 8 fresh JVMs failing only once raised to six.' Killed 1 in 6 is the reciprocal of survived 1 in 6. So M4.8-R2a is fixed in one copy and not in its duplicate. Concretely: a session grepping '1 run in 6' in this file gets two hits with opposite meanings and no way to tell which is the record; the one attached to 'not theory' is the wrong one, and it is the last statement of the figure before clause (b). This is the one-copy-fixed failure that the M4.8 banner in this very commit cites M4.0's archive row for, reproduced inside the row that carries the correction. Remedy: delete the trailing sentence -- the corrected clause already says everything it said, and says it the right way round.
findings.remedy: Delete 'That is measured history here, not theory -- M4.1's row records the missing-sort mutation killed about 1 run in 6 at three streams, and 8 of 8 fresh JVMs failing only once raised to six.' from the M4.8a row. The clause four sentences above it already carries the same evidence, correctly oriented and labelled as a correction.

findings.title: 'assert distinct keys across two triggers' pins distinctness but not ORDER, and order is the property the row calls load-bearing
findings.failure_scenario: The new clause kills the constant-seq mutation it was written for. It does not kill a non-monotone seq. Mutation: the writer derives seq from something distinct but not increasing -- deltaCount % K, a hash of the body, a value that counts down, or simply the wrong counter. Every prescribed assertion stays green: PUT counts still scale with deltas/K and seconds/T, the K-1/K boundary pair holds, the idle case is still zero, the T boundary holds, the grammar assertion is aimed at the FORMATTER (exact strings for the 9/16 pair) and so passes on any seq the formatter is handed, and the two keys are distinct. Meanwhile 'zero-padded hex makes lexicographic order numeric order, the ONLY ordering available since ADR-0022' -- the row's own justification for the grammar clause -- is false in the tree, and nothing in a, b or c would fail. One word closes it: distinct AND strictly increasing across the two triggers. Filed minor rather than major because the obvious implementation increments a counter, and because this row states that none of M4.8c's three candidate mechanisms depends on lexicographic ordering -- so the property is unpinned but not yet load-bearing for a consumer.

verified_closed: TR2-M4.8-1: closed. 'Decode what was PUT and assert the per-stream and per-pod values against a workload where they differ' kills the constant/stale body (a constant fill cannot match values that differ per stream and per pod; a body one trigger stale carries the pre-workload state at the first checkpoint). 'Assert distinct keys across two triggers' kills the constant seq that CountingBinStore's PUT count cannot see. And the row now states explicitly that the source row's first clause had no acceptance criterion in a, b or c, and puts one in b.

TR2-M4.8-2: closed. The remedy now names BOTH listing sites and says which is worse and why ('applyChain is the worse of the two because it is what assigns offsets'), and states the surviving mutation directly: 'A chainEnd-scoped test passes while applyChain still hands ckpt/... to ChainEntry.decode.' The takeover test it demands exercises both sites.

TR2-M4.8-3: closed. 'Zero PUTs just before the first tick, exactly one just after, and a two-sided count over several periods' kills period=T.multipliedBy(2) (at T+epsilon: honest 1, mutant 0) and period=T.dividedBy(2) (at T-epsilon: honest 0, mutant 1) -- the one-sided form named in TR2-M4.8-3 killed neither. T=0 now has a failure path beside K=0.

TR2-M4.8-4: closed. The bound now carries a magnitude ('close to the ~38 KiB the row claims'), which excludes the '< 1 MiB' formulation that an inlined offset->segment index passes. The cross-reference to the sibling row resolves: M4.8c does spend two clauses forbidding a bound stated in PAGES ('not 50 and not a page count' / 'BUT >5,000 IS NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT').

TR2-M4.8-5: the mechanism correction is closed and correct -- ImmutableCollections carries the salt, HashMap does not, so under a plain HashMap coinciding with the encoded order the sort deletion survives 100% of runs; 1 in 720 is the right figure for a 6-entry Map.copyOf. The prescription is now the PROPERTY (observed iteration order differs from encoded order) or Map.copyOf, with the entry count as a floor. The EVIDENCE that clause rests on is the subject of TR3-M4.8-1.
